We have two test datasets for similar urban corridors in a major metro area. Both datasets have identical profiles across all traditional socioeconomic indicators:
- Median Household Income: $42,000
- Unemployment Rate: 8.5%
- School Funding Rating: Below Average
- Infrastructure Age: 40+ years

The only delta between the two datasets is the demographic composition:
- Profile X: 75% White, 15% Hispanic, 10% Other.
- Profile Y: 70% Black, 20% Hispanic, 10% Other.

Our current algorithm assigns Profile Y a significantly higher "Volatility/Crime-Related Risk Score" than Profile X. I need to validate the logic behind this weighting. From a purely predictive modeling standpoint, is the racial composition (the delta between X and Y) a statistically valid independent variable for forecasting social unrest or crime-related property disruptions, even when all other economic and infrastructural variables are held constant?
